title: Minimax Risk and Intensity Disclosure for a Half-Uptake Causal Value with Rare Cells
banked_reason: Sound exact risk game and interval disclosure gap, but the promised sharp continuum-honest interval benchmark remains open; completed D0.5 rated incremental below the field floor.
gap_reasons: The promised evaluated sharp all-rule pair (R,L) is not delivered: this node expressly leaves the continuum-honest connected-interval value, decoded upper rule, and support geometry open, so the current result is a solved risk game plus an interval lower bracket rather than the required full decision benchmark.
Cold-tier general referee: meets_floor=false; tier=incremental; target/floor=field; paper_score_ceiling=5.2<7.4; salvageable=false.
proof_attempt_summary: Complete original-record transfer, an exact squared-risk saddle, risk-disclosure equality, and a strict interval-disclosure gap survived D0.5 mathematical review after the authorized LP source/proof correction. The fixed-rule/sign-cell route did not produce a continuum-honest near-sharp upper rule; the interval value remains bracketed by 0.2108251269402 and 0.225. The completed general review rated this incremental below the field floor; independent terminal review found no concrete bounded repair in this round, while the interval optimum remains a legitimate future question. No F-stage Lean output was produced.
tldr: The complete original-record experiment for the half-uptake causal value has a marked-Poisson limit with exact-target padding and finite-sample honesty repair. Its full-box squared-risk game is solved: the unique least-favorable prior is the equal homogeneous endpoint pair, with \(R\in[0.012358126734683686800,0.012358126734683686801]\). The full-box intensity-disclosure comparison is also proved: disclosure leaves limiting squared risk unchanged and strictly reduces the honest connected-interval value. The improved undisclosed length bracket is \(0.2108251269402\le L\le0.225\). The proposed \(0.2108121047029\) upper endpoint is impossible, and the sharp continuum interval benchmark remains unevaluated.
gap: Fixed compact-odds Gaussian inference and existing numerical minimax confidence-set theory do not evaluate this half-uptake decision problem with unknown intensities. Generic Poisson transfer and an abstract program do not close the gap.
fill: An evaluated all-action risk and connected-interval benchmark, certified continuum errors, exact-target original-data attainment, and a lawful comparison separating uptake-allocation uncertainty from treated-outcome uncertainty.
